data.narrative:
Telexistence, a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jin Tomioka and Ken Tomoyose, has raised $170M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 3 same-stage private comparables in the robotics sector (Generalist AI at $2.0B, Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B, and Dexterity at $1.6B), supplemented by a broader universe of 8 private peers and 1 public comparable.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method, using total capital raised ($170M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yields $323M. The peer-median approach anchors to the three same-sector, same-stage comparables, producing a median valuation of $1.8B (range: $1.6B–$2.0B). These methods produce substantially divergent outputs, reflecting the wide dispersion in robotics company valuations at this stage.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $275M to $2.0B, with a median of $1.0B. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty around whether Telexistence should trade toward earlier-stage fundamentals (stage-progression) or command peer-equivalent multiples on operational traction not detailed in available data. Resolution hinges on revenue scale, customer concentration, and technological differentiation relative to the three named peers. Additional disclosure on unit economics and TAM penetration would narrow this range substantially.
